chunks: I wrote to him (peace be upon him) regarding a man who sold a garden of his that contained trees and a vineyard, and he excepted one tree from it. Is he entitled to a passage to the garden to reach the location of the tree he excepted? And how much of the surrounding land belongs to this excepted tree: is it according to the spread of its branches, or according to the spot where it is growing? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He has that according to what he sold and kept, so he does not exceed the right in that, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of access and land extent when a tree is excepted from a sold garden?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Hasan (AS) clarifies the jurisprudence of partial exclusion (*istithna'*) in property sales, specifically addressing the right of way (*mamarr*) and the spatial extent of an excepted tree. The Imam’s response emphasizes proportional equity, ensuring that the buyer’s retained rights do not infringe upon the seller’s remaining property, a principle foundational to Shia commercial law. This ruling underscores the importance of precise boundary definition to prevent disputes (*ta'addi*) in real estate transactions.
